materials: unit-specific source, model, manipulatives, safe materials, or approved digital tool

Household-accessible route: pencil or pen and scrap paper are enough. For sound or performance work, tap, clap, use spoken syllables, move a finger, or notate silently. Specialized art materials, instruments, paid software, cameras, microphones, and recording devices are optional and never affect credit.
task_brief: Project work on scene structure. Project: plan, select, sequence, document, test, and revise a sustained body of work through scene structure, then use observable evidence to explain or revise a learner-owned decision. Complete the bounded study yourself before asking for a cue.
primary_task: Target for this increment session: Create, test, or revise a meaningful product that applies scene structure and the unit standards. Use subject-appropriate evidence or representation to communicate understanding of scene structure. Check, revise, or improve work about scene structure using stated success criteria. Closing evidence check: In one concise response, show or explain the most important idea about scene structure; then identify one check that would catch an error or weak claim. What scene structure means here: A portfolio or project is a purposeful sequence of work and decisions, not simply a pile of finished pieces. 1. Milestone plan: Define today’s purpose, available materials, non-negotiable constraints, learner-owned choices, and the evidence that will mark this scene structure milestone complete. 2. Project build: Complete one reviewable project increment using scene structure. Record the starting state, today’s bounded finish, a criteria check, and one learner-chosen revision. 3. Critique: Describe before judging. Locate evidence, compare it with the maker’s stated intent, ask one genuine question, and offer options; the maker keeps final authority. A private self-critique receives full credit. 4. Revision: Change one relationship in response to a named criterion. Preserve the earlier version and explain why the change better serves—or intentionally changes—the stated intent. Your choices remain yours: Different project question, items to develop or select, private presentation format, sequence, revision and next-step priorities choices are valid when the learner meets objective constraints and supports the result with evidence. Keep today's work tied to your unit. Today is about scene structure. It is part of "Theater, Storytelling, and Movement". Later days in this unit cover other things, like character and objective. Before you stop, do this check: In one concise response, show or explain the most important idea about scene structure; then identify one check that would catch an error or weak claim. In grade 4, try the steps yourself before you ask for help. Give a reason in your own words for at least one choice. A labelled drawing or a spoken answer counts fully.

presentation_and_privacy.presentation_options: You choose the audience. Keeping the work entirely to yourself, showing it to one parent or trusted adult, or submitting it as a file with no one watching are all full-credit options. No public performance, exhibition, class presentation, live audience, photograph, camera, or voice recording is required at any point in this task, and choosing the most private option never lowers the score.
presentation_and_privacy.text_or_no_audio_alternative: A written alternative is always available for spoken reflection, explanation, or critique and scores the same. Use a written analysis, labelled plan, evidence table, notation, diagram, or private artifact check that preserves the stated target. No microphone, camera, recording, or public audience is required.

copyright_and_authorship: The graded submission must be your own authorship. A parent, tutor, or AI tool may explain an idea, demonstrate a technique, or give feedback on a draft, but must not produce, write, debug, or make any part of the work that is scored. Any material you did not create yourself must be in the public domain, openly licensed, or used as a short cited excerpt for study — reproduce no more than the point requires, credit the maker and the source, and never copy full lyrics, a complete score, or a whole image and present it as your own.
accessibility_options: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, manipulatives-based, or demonstrated responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.
task_accessibility_provisions: You never have to perform in front of people. Showing one trusted grown-up, or just writing about it, counts the same.
This work takes more than one sitting. Ask for a simple checklist with dates so you know what to do next. Keeping track is not part of your grade.
You can take a break, stretch, or come back to this later. That does not lower your score.
safety_and_privacy_rules: Allow a pause, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Protect hearing, ventilation, tool safety, copyright, cultural context, and respectful representation.
No public performance, voice recording, photo, or camera use is ever required; provide a private, written, or no-audio alternative for every task.
Use only original student work, public-domain material, or properly licensed excerpts; never reproduce full copyrighted lyrics, sheet music, or protected works.
The final product must remain the student’s own authorship; adult or AI assistance may support planning and feedback but must not create the graded work.

media.suggestion: Optional diagram, map, worked example, source image, demonstration, or short clip supporting scene structure.
media.fallback: Provide the same information as readable steps, alt text, transcript, tactile/concrete model, or teacher demonstration.

remediation: Route 1: Reduce scene structure to three locatable events, areas, steps, or decisions. Label the intended effect beside each and underline the one purpose relationship that should carry it. Use a separate small study, four-event loop, thumbnail, evidence table, or paper plan. The adult may model the noticing process on different material but may not change the learner’s work. Check yourself: Point to or name the exact purpose evidence before deciding whether it serves the intent. New attempt: Put the support away and make a new arrangement, passage, response, or plan; record what the new evidence shows. Route 2: Return to the last understandable state. Hold every relationship steady except one chosen feature from purpose, milestone, artifact record, decision trail, rights note, criteria check, and next step; predict what that single change should do. Test the feature on scrap paper, a silent count, a two-event rehearsal loop, movable shapes, or a short evidence sentence before changing the scored work. Check yourself: Name what stayed the same, what changed, and the first observable result—without using “better” as the evidence. New attempt: Create a different small case using the same one-variable method, then transfer the finding to the original task only if it serves the learner’s intent.
extension: Apply scene structure under a new constraint, compare two approaches or perspectives, or teach the idea with an original example without completing another learner’s graded work. Treat this as optional depth on scene structure rather than extra volume: one harder case done well beats three more of the same. Extension work stays private by default and uses only original, public-domain, or properly cited material. Extension work is never required to reach mastery and must not be assigned as a penalty.

concept_instruction.title: What scene structure means here
concept_instruction.body: A portfolio or project is a purposeful sequence of work and decisions, not simply a pile of finished pieces.

concept_instruction.title: How the relationship changes the result
concept_instruction.body: Selection and sequencing create an argument about growth or purpose; process evidence makes revisions and authorship traceable without continuous surveillance.

concept_instruction.title: Choice and tradeoff
concept_instruction.body: More items can show range but weaken focus. Fewer items can create coherence but must provide enough evidence for the stated goal. Worked example: A three-item sequence—question, experiment, revision—can reveal a clearer process than ten unrelated polished pieces. Non-example: Choosing only favourites without criteria does not explain why the group belongs together.

technique_sequence.action: State the intended effect or question before making or judging.
technique_sequence.notice: The statement creates a criterion that can be checked.
technique_sequence.why: Arts evidence is interpreted in relation to purpose, not personal taste.

technique_sequence.action: Identify or set up the relevant purpose, milestone, artifact record, decision trail, rights note, criteria check, and next step.
technique_sequence.notice: Locate the first relationship that can be observed in scene structure.
technique_sequence.why: Selection and sequencing create an argument about growth or purpose; process evidence makes revisions and authorship traceable without continuous surveillance.

technique_sequence.action: Complete one small controlled study or rehearsal loop.
technique_sequence.notice: Keep most relationships stable so one decision remains readable.
technique_sequence.why: A bounded test makes cause and effect easier to notice.

technique_sequence.action: Transfer the idea to a fresh work, excerpt, source detail, or project decision.
technique_sequence.notice: Close the model or cue before the independent decision.

technique_sequence.action: Check against criteria and choose a revision or a reasoned decision to keep the result.
technique_sequence.notice: Cite a location, moment, event, or process fact before judging.
technique_sequence.why: Evidence protects creative variation and learner authority.

common_technique_errors.observable_mismatch: The stated intent for scene structure is present, but the record does not yet locate purpose, milestone, artifact record, decision trail, rights note, criteria check, and next step that supports it.
common_technique_errors.not_an_error_when: The learner supports a different, ambiguous, subtle, or intentionally open effect with observable evidence.

common_technique_errors.observable_mismatch: Several relationships changed at once, so the learner cannot yet tell which choice caused the observed effect.
common_technique_errors.not_an_error_when: The task is an intentionally exploratory diagnostic and no causal claim is being scored.
